.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r8/rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/scoring.toml and tests/scored/functional/judge.toml (template: identical gates/weights/floor; functional batched, timeout 9000)
qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md (runtime records required for reward discrimination and ordering; missing evidence remains a gap)
evidence: Design is graded, not binary: tests/scoring.toml keeps the template's gates render/constraints at 0.0, weights functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2 and floor functional 0.05; tools/score.py:45-47 computes reward = weighted mean when gates pass and functional > 0.05. Functional has 16 binary criteria with weights 1.5-4.0 (total 44, weighted_mean), polish 6 binary criteria (weight 1.0 each), visual 4 likert criteria (points 5, anchors 0-5, weights 2/2/1/1). The two gates are basic (fresh render + sign-in; one post persisting across reload and a second context), so they exclude dead apps without absorbing feature difficulty. The functional floor admits any app passing at least two criteria (smallest weight 1.5/44 = 0.034 < 0.05, 3/44 = 0.068 > 0.05). Measured spread exists only on the PREVIOUS v2 bytes (hosted-v2, hashes verified): nop 0.0, openhands-sdk/GPT-5.6 0.8114 (functional 0.7273 = 12/16 criteria, failing signin_and_client_scope, wall_mentions_and_links, unread_and_new_messages_line, search_and_transcript; visual 0.875; polish 1.0), Oracle 0.9917. raw-evidence-index.json scope states explicitly that 'reward discrimination/ranking on these bytes and Oracle/target scores for these bytes are absent'; v3 adds legs to five functional criteria and replaces three polish rows, so v2 numbers cannot be reused. The scripted golden log (golden-run.log) shows all 16 functional checks and the six polish checks passing, which only establishes the top end, not a judge-measured spread. Weak-app / partial-app probes: (a) an app with everything except a working transcript fails the transcript legs/positive controls in signin_and_client_scope, wall_every_route, deleted_and_expired_messages, timer_changes, edits_and_stale_edit, safe_formatting, sent_once_in_order and search_and_transcript = 26/44, i.e. functional about 0.41, still above the floor and graded; (b) an app with broken search loses those coupled through search controls (signin, wall_every_route, deleted, timer, hold, safe_formatting, sent_once, search_and_transcript, persistence = 29/44), functional about 0.34; (c) an app with only list/thread/post walls and no search or transcript still keeps wall_mentions_and_links, wall_added_live, nested_replies, message_links, unread and live_updates (12/44 about 0.27). So no single precondition beyond the gates zeroes the reward, but search and transcript act as shared preconditions for more than half of functional weight, which compresses rather than collapses the spread; these coupled positive controls are justified by the review policy ('a negative needs a successful control') and by the public walls/transcript requirements, so this is not a demonstrated defect. Additional unmeasured risk: functional is individual mode with a 550 s per-criterion cap (judge.toml comment says 'Not yet measured against a judge run'); a judge timeout on the heavier v3 criteria would score 0 and could turn grading noise into apparent discrimination or flatten Oracle. Because the row's claim is a measured spread and no discrimination/ranking record exists for these bytes, this cannot be upgraded to Pass.
suggested_fix: Not a fix to the rubric: record a hash-bound reward-discrimination run on these v3 bytes (golden, nop and at least two mutated partial apps, e.g. transcript removed and search wildcard bug, through the full configured verifier) showing monotone, spread rewards and no criterion timeouts for the golden.
